segments.title: Chương 167: Diễn đàn nhà văn
segments.content:
Chapter 170: 0167 Writer's Forum (Bonus Chapter for Alliance Leader 99玖玖久久)

An event jointly organized by *Mengya* and the Shanghai Writers' Association was called the "First Literary Intergenerational Communication Forum."

They invited writers from the old, middle-aged, and young generations to sit together and talk about literary creation.

The event would last for a week. The first day was a get-together in the Magic City, and the remaining six days would be at Thousand Island Lake.

Of course, Chen Guiliang wasn't going to Thousand Island Lake. His agreeing to attend the opening ceremony in the Magic City was already giving *Mengya* a lot of face.

*Mengya* Magazine Agency.

President Zhao Changtian asked, "Is Chen Guiliang confirmed to be coming?"

"Yes, but only for the first day," Hu Weishi said. "He's not going to Thousand Island Lake, says it's too much of a time commitment."

Zhao Changtian nodded and said, "It's good enough that he can attend the opening ceremony. After all, he doesn't rely on writing books to make money anymore. What about Han Han?"

Hu Weishi said, "He has a car race, can't get away. He really can't. He even called me last night to apologize."

"What about Guo Xiao Si?" Zhao Changtian asked Li Qigang.

He asked Li Qigang because Hu Weishi and Guo Xiao Si had a falling out, so this time, only Li Qigang could extend the invitation.

Li Qigang gave a wry smile. "The first time I called him, he said he had to discuss it with his agent. The second time I called, he said he had to discuss it with his image consultant. I've been in this business for so many years, and it's the first time I've heard of a writer having an agent and an image consultant."

Zhao Changtian frowned. "Isn't he putting on too many airs?"

"It's not that he's putting on airs," Li Qigang said with great certainty. "He doesn't dare to come. His reputation is shot, and he's afraid of getting chewed out. I spoke with his agent, and the agent has been trying to persuade him. Guess who his agent is?"

"Who is it?" Hu Weishi asked curiously.

Li Qigang smiled. "The Deputy Editor-in-Chief of Changjiang Literature and Art Publishing House, Jin Lihong."

"The Deputy Editor-in-Chief of Changjiang Literature and Art is Guo Xiao Si's agent?" Zhao Changtian and Hu Weishi were both flabbergasted.

This Jin Lihong was a major veteran in the publishing industry.

She had led the planning for books by authors including Wang Shuo, Liu Zhenyun, Jiang Wen, Bai Yansong, Cui Yongyuan, Yu Qiuyu, and Hai Yan.

Li Qigang said, "This Jin Lihong is very capable. I can guess what she's trying to do. She plans to use all the resources at her disposal to help Guo Xiao Si eliminate his negative image. This event is an opportunity to connect with the Shanghai Writers' Association, and the next step would be to get Guo Xiao Si to join the association. But Guo Xiao Si is still too green, and overly insecure. He simply doesn't dare to come and meet fellow writers."

"I don't care if he comes or not. He actually sent me a text cursing me out!" Hu Weishi said irritably.

Literary Forum, Opening Ceremony.

Not many writers came, fewer than 40 in total.

Sixty-one-year-old Cheng Cun arrived at the venue, leaning on a crutch.

He suffered from ankylosing spondylitis and had been walking hunched over with a crutch for many years.

During that soccer match where they had Shi Tiesheng be the goalkeeper, Cheng Cun had also been there, acting as the referee from the sidelines, leaning on his crutch.

"The Fire expansion generals for *Legends of the Three Kingdoms Online* are coming out!" Cheng Cun said as soon as he saw Yu Hua.

Yu Hua replied perfunctorily, "Is that so?"

Cheng Cun questioned, "You haven't been playing recently, have you? Even Ah Cheng logs on often. Ah Cheng steals my crops every day now."

"Steals crops?" Yu Hua didn't understand.

"*Happy Farm*," Cheng Cun said.

What on earth was Happy Farm?

Yu Hua looked at the white-haired Cheng Cun, wondering if he himself had fallen behind the times.

It wasn't that he had fallen behind, but that Cheng Cun was too trendy.

This old writer surfed the internet every day. Later, when Han Han battled Bai Ye and Fang Zhouzi, he, at his advanced age, jumped into the fray, standing by Han Han's side and engaging in online flame wars the entire time. In the first battle, he offended many writers in the circle; in the second, he was relentlessly flamed by Fang Zhouzi's fans.

More and more young writers arrived, and Cheng Cun hobbled over. "Which of you plays *Happy Farm*?"

"Huh?" Zhang Yueran and the others were a bit bewildered.

Ma Zhongcai, a writer from the post-80s generation, weakly raised his hand. "I do."

Cheng Cun handed him a small notebook. "Write down your Youke account. I'll add you as a friend later."

Ma Zhongcai scratched his head, feeling that something was off.

Li Haiyang said, "Teacher Cheng Cun, I steal crops too, but I do it on Xiaonei. Hehe, you can't register for a Xiaonei account."

Cheng Cun couldn't be bothered with him and asked the others, "None of you steal crops?"

Everyone shook their heads.

After Cheng Cun left, Song Jingru, an editor for *Chinese National Geography* magazine, asked, "What is 'stealing crops'?"

Liu Lina, a post-80s female writer, shook her head. "I don't know."

Zhou Jianing, currently a master's student at Fudan, said, "It's a casual game, available on Xiaonei. I was addicted to it for over a month, too, and even paid for a membership."

The suspense novelist Cai Jun asked, "Is that the website owned by that Chen Guiliang?"

"Yeah," Ma Zhongcai said. "Didn't you recommend his *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty* on your blog?"

Cai Jun explained, "Li Xunhuan asked me to recommend it, as a way of returning a favor. I've never even met Chen Guiliang, nor have I read his book. It seems he's gotten popular again recently, became some kind of multi-millionaire."

Zhang Yueran, who had just returned to China after graduating from a university in Singapore, was completely out of the loop. "Who is Chen Guiliang?"

Li Haiyang said, "Same as me, a first-prize winner of the 6th New Concept Writing Competition. His historical novel *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty* is selling very well. I estimate that in another month, sales will break one million copies."

"That's very impressive," said Zhang Yueran.

Zhao Yan, who had now changed his pen name to Naduo, also came and sat down. "He's also running a company. He got venture capital funding a while ago, and the shares in his name are valued at 160 million. Sigh, it's just completely unimaginable. Back in November of the year before last, I even reviewed his preliminary contest manuscript. He was just a third-year high school student back then."

Zhang Yueran found it even harder to comprehend. "What kind of company did he start?"

Zhou Jianing said, "Xiaonei, a campus social networking site. All the students in my graduate program are Xiaonei users."

The post-80s female writer Yan Ge said, "This guy is from our Sichuan province. The *West China Metropolis Daily* loves to report on him. Oh, and he's a high school alumnus of Guo Xiao Si."

"Is Guo Xiao Si coming today?"

"Who cares if he comes."

"What about Chen Guiliang?"

"Seems like he's coming. Han Han is confirmed not to be, he's busy with car racing."

"Look, Xiao Fan and Jiang Feng are here!"

Chen Guiliang arrived right on time. He had gone out for skewers with two high school classmates last night.

One was his Room 302 roommate, Li Dongqiang, who was studying at a second-tier university in the Magic City. The other was a classmate from before the arts and sciences streams were separated, studying electrical engineering at the University of Shanghai for Science and Technology. Neither of them had gone home for the summer break.

He got half-drunk and slept until the sun was high in the sky.

Sitting in a taxi, Chen Guiliang received a call from Ao Yanchen. "QQ Zone has officially launched. Except for a few features like groups, almost all the other functions are identical to our Xiaonei."

"Shi Qian and the others are already on their way back with the contract," Chen Guiliang instructed. "Plan an event properly with Tudou. Encourage Xiaonei users to self-record videos, upload them to Tudou, and then embed them into Xiaonei. The people from Tudou will communicate the specific event details with Xie Yang. Also, speed up the promotion of Xiaonei in high schools."

"When are you coming back?" Ao Yanchen asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm flying to Rongcheng tonight. I have to make a trip home. I should be back at the company next week."

"You're certainly taking it easy."

"It's about letting the team gel. When I get back, I'll see how well you've all meshed."

In the past few months, the Chinese internet had developed rapidly.

Last month, for the first time, the number of netizens using broadband internet surpassed those using dial-up.

Moreover, compared to the beginning of the year, in just three short months, online payment had become more and more mature. The number of online shoppers increased rapidly, with the media even using the phrase "online shopping craze" to describe it.

had reached nearly 400 million—cell phone prices had plummeted this year.

The model of phone Chen Guiliang was currently using could be bought for just five hundred yuan.

Consequently, SMS-based top-up payments were also becoming more and more common.

All these factors led to a huge increase in profits for both the online version and physical card game of *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*!

As someone who had lived through this before, Chen Guiliang felt this change most deeply. China at this time was truly advancing at a phenomenal pace.

Oh, and there was one more thing.

Twelve days after Chen Guiliang received his investment, JD.com officially went online...

"Chen Guiliang!" Hu Weishi, who was waiting outside the venue, waved at him.
